The author states a decided schedule: the Category III CPT codes for fMRI-guided accelerated neuromodulation 'go into effect on July 1st'. The AMA CPT Editorial Panel publishes Category III codes before their effective date, and the author reports the codes as already issued. The outcome was publicly determined by the deciding body on the statement date.

'Good luck keeping that private and proprietary' implies that DRG multipliers will not stay secret, but names no payer, no event, no threshold, no resolution source and no date. Footnote aside; no observable event can be written.

Expectation ('it's really hard to imagine you're gonna adopt') that per-diem psychiatric hospitals do not adopt novel stay-shortening treatments such as SAINT. No countable set of hospitals, no threshold, no named data series and no date. The finder's hint (a SAINT installation list cross-referenced with contracting type) is not a series the forecaster named and would have to be invented.

Metaphor ('GLP-1s are a shot across the bow'; 'sugar and pharma are no longer in sync'). No entity decision, event, threshold or date can be written. Also outside the five areas (food industry versus pharma).

Readership growth of the author's own newsletter ('a ton more readers') is not a regulatory, trial, company or market, payer or policy, or practice-adoption outcome. 'A ton more' also has no benchmark, and the light-hearted framing is close to satire.

'Will eventually deliver us from the purgatory of crappy treatments for PTSD' covers a class of compounds (MDMA, ibogaine, psilocybin and others), names no regulator decision, trial or benchmark, and 'eventually' is not a deadline. No observable event can be written.
Publishing plan for the author's own newsletter series (a next-day post and a 'path forward' by series end). A publication of the forecaster's own organization; the author decides the outcome.

Statement of preference: MBT 'would be a great therapy manual for combination with a compound like MDMA'. A hypothetical design proposal; no future state, decision or date is asserted.

FALSE on the date of the first such approval that has no REMS. TRUE at the window end if every such approval carried a REMS.
